review.verdict: Fails: the worker overlaps and clips the PAUSED label and stop sign, the thermometer meter spills outside the safe area per the lint warning, and the 'half-built datacenter with frozen cranes' and ballot symbol don't read as described, leaving the left half's joke muddled next to the clearer robot side.
revisionNotes: The worker (human, x:0.46,y:0.74, scale 0.85) overlaps the stopsign and label-paused, cutting 'PAUSED' to 'PAUS'. Move worker to beside the datacenter instead of on top of the stop sign, or shrink to scale 0.6 and shift stopsign to x:0.3 so they don't collide.

Lint confirms the meter (attached right of robot) clips outside the safe area at x:982-1070. Reduce offset from [40,-100] to [10,-80] or scale the meter to 0.8 so it sits fully inside the 1080 canvas.
The datacenter component reads as a small filing cabinet, not a half-built site with frozen cranes per the brief. Scale it up to 1.3 and add a simple crane-boom raw prop so 'frozen mid-lift' reads.

The stop sign shows a checkmark, not a ballot symbol, so the election-loss link doesn't land. Swap the raw SVG checkmark for a ballot-box slot or X-in-a-box shape.

Composition leans on a beige/teal horizontal split rather than the brief's vertical divider contrasting frozen left vs fast right. Add a thin vertical divider line at x:0.5 to sharpen the two-halves contrast.

review.verdict: The pause-vs-speed split reads at a glance, but the brief's actual joke — a robot bolting together a faster copy of itself — never appears (it just stands smiling with arms out), the PAUSED label overlaps the data center, and the divider/data center bleed past the safe area; this needs another pass before it's publish-ready.
revisionNotes: Add the actual metaphor: give the robot a 'holds: tool' prop and a second, smaller mirror-robot component on the bench so it reads as bolting together a faster copy of itself — right now it just stands with arms out and smiles.
Move or shrink the 'PAUSED' label so it clears the datacenter's right edge/door panel; currently it overlaps the white door lines and gets lost in the pattern.
Shorten the divider's height (currently 1080, edge to edge) so it sits inside the safe area instead of bleeding off the top and bottom per the lint warning.
Pull the datacenter in from the left edge — drop scale from 1.3 to ~1.15 or shift anchor x from 0.25 to ~0.28 so it clears the safe-area margin the lint flagged (x 48…492).

Make the stop sign's ballot link legible: the X-in-a-box currently reads as a generic 'closed' icon, not an election symbol — add a simple ballot-slot or checkbox shape so the election connection isn't lost.
Pull worker2's raised arm back or shift its anchor right so the hand doesn't visually fuse with the stop sign pole.

review.verdict: A clean, well-cast split composition that clears the bar, but the central metaphor — the robot bolting together a faster copy of itself — doesn't actually read as an action, and the ballot symbol on the stop sign is too subtle to connect to the election beat.
revisionNotes: The robot's 'bolting together a faster copy of itself' doesn't read as an action — the mini-robot just sits passively on the bench with no visible connection. Angle the bolt-tool toward the mini-robot and tilt the big robot forward so the assembly beat is legible.
The bolt-tool in the robot's left hand reads as a plain teal ball, not a bolt — redraw it as a visible hex-bolt or wrench shape and scale to ~1.1 so the prop is identifiable.
The stop sign's checkmark-in-box reads as 'approved', not 'ballot' — redraw the raw shape as a ballot slipping into a slot (per the brief) so the election cue is unambiguous.
The speed meter uses a thermometer component, which cues temperature rather than speed — swap to a dial/gauge kind so 'twice as fast' reads instantly.

Vertical-divider split compositions with a human side vs robot side have shown up repeatedly in recent sloppers (Stock Falls/Jobs Cut, CATASTROPHIC RISK) — vary the layout (e.g., diagonal split or overlapping frame) for more novelty next time.
Anchor the crane hook directly to the datacenter roofline instead of floating above it, so the 'frozen mid-lift' read is clearer.
